title.label: Fantastic tool, can it do more?

content.label:
This is my most used app across my devices, helping manage projects, to-dos and generally organising my work life. The streamlined interface and simple design really allow your tasks to be front and centre. 

There are some things that I’d love to see come to future versions of the app:
- the ability to add headings within areas, just like you can in projects. This would be really useful to separate out tasks within areas that don’t fall in to a specific project
- expand the ‘Today’ and ‘This Evening’ feature so include ‘This Morning’ and ‘This Afternoon’. This would help to better layout a day of tasks
- finally, the ability to create templates for projects. I have several projects that occur regularly, and while I have a template set up, this exists as just another project in the app. It would be great to have a separate menu or filter to store these templates

I can’t fault the app, these are ideas that could take it even further

I’m a planner, and i’m seriously disappointed I can’t put in dates for things I have to do in months of a time. Also, you can’t even see the calendar at full view to see what you have on that month, you have to scroll along. I’ll be enquiring about a refund asap.
Great app but unfortunately I cannot easily use it as it does not adhere to the system font size settings. If you have to increase the font size of your iPhone then this app isn’t for you.

This has got to be one of the better reminders apps I’ve used (which is a lot of them). The notifications are very good and the project organisation is pretty solid. My only criticism would be a lack of customisation for the Today view. I’d like to be able to give tags a geolocation so I don’t have to select them and more support for custom views like in omnifocus but otherwise this app is fantastic.

title.label: Close to perfect with room for improvement

content.label:
I seldom write reviews on the App Store unless an app is truly exceptional and Things 3 is just one of those apps. Truthfully, if I could I’d give this app 4.5/5 if that were possible, but docking an entire star for the reasons I have feels a bit unfair considering the impact it’s had on my daily life. Perhaps you have reservations about the price tag; I did too but I’m pleased to say it was worth every penny. It’s perhaps the only app that has actually increased my productivity almost instantaneously. I used to use Evernote for my todo list and I noticed that even though I was writing things down, I wasn’t getting them done. Instead they’d just sit there often getting lost as I made newer notes. Because Things is designed to get you completing tasks instead of just writing about them, there are powerful features to support this, such as badges that tell you how many tasks you have for the day when you aren’t in the app, and easy ways of creating new tasks and moving them around. It removes a lot of the anxiety that comes from having a busy day and not knowing what to tackle first. 
That being said, no app is perfect and I have three key suggestions for the developers on where to improve. 

- It would be great if there were some kind of quick swipe action or even a button to quickly move something to tomorrow. 

- Being able to select anytime in the same menu as someday when changing the date of a task would be very useful (currently the only way is to go to search, type anytime, then tap anytime when it comes up, which isn’t very intuitive). 

- Badges show up for everything you have to do today, regardless of whether it set to today or this evening. it would be good if there were a way to add a custom rule to badge count to only display badges based on the time of day (e.g) you have 3 todos today, 4 this evening making 7 in total. Instead of showing 7, there should be an option to show 3, then 4 later.

2 months in. So far, so superuseful.
Frictionless and (mostly) distraction free (No pictures or links or attachments). Superb reminders and calendar integration. Responsive, intelligent developers.
Initial outlay takes commitment, but is fair and much preferable to other’s subscription model. That does sometimes feels like fishing for the unorganised who forget to cancel.

I suspect paying up front for iOS, later adding iPadOS, lately MacOS seems to keep me sticking with it. I‘m chronically indecisive and used to hop from one system to the next.

Catching fleeting thoughts in Inbox and perusing them later is hugely enjoyable, so is organising them.
Ticking off even the tiniest tasks rewards adding them in the first place.

It‘s become my ADHD‘s first beneficial addiction. :)

I’ve been in and out of Mac Calendar, Reminders, Notes and Daytimer pen and paper diary for years and it’s been driving me nuts. This app has brought it all together into one. I’ve got a busy year ahead and the Upcoming feature of this app shows everything going on. The To Do add in is clean and so uncomplicated that it’s a pleasure to get the thought into the app and make it happen with no pressure or silly red overdue warnings.It could do with just a little bit more going on for the Apple Watch but otherwise excellent!
Great handy app to keep organised
